title: Year three close: the long story
hookLine: from the cave of Hira to your nearest mosque, fourteen centuries of people
carry: you are in the story now

cards: Read. Tradition says that word came to a man alone in the dark, in a cave on a mountain above Mecca, and would not let him go. Now, a mosque on an ordinary street near you.
Shoes in a rack by the door. A child running between the rows before the prayer starts. An older man folding a prayer mat.
Between that cave and this doorway lie century after century of people, and this year has tried to meet them. Before a new year opens, a look back down the road.

teach.b: On the first day of this year, your line was: people carried it. Here is who carried it. First, the Prophet ﷺ himself, in full.
Mecca before the revelation. The orphan, the trader, Khadijah's husband. The cave, and the command that came there, in Pickthall's translation: "Read: In the name of thy Lord who createth."
The years of persecution, the sorrow, Ta'if, the night journey, the road to Yathrib, and Medina.
Second, those who walked beside him. The first circle. The mothers of the believers.
His family. The freed slave who called the prayer, the women who asked hard questions. Third, the hard chapter.
The succession, the caliphs, the first split, and Karbala, told with Sunni and Shia memory side by side, neither one ranked.

teach.h: THE LONG ROAD, CITY BY CITY.
teach.b: Fourth, the long road after. Damascus and Baghdad, al-Andalus and Cairo, Timbuktu and Samarkand, Istanbul, Isfahan, Delhi, Java, China.

teach.h: READ: IN THE NAME OF THY LORD WHO CREATETH.
teach.b: Scholars, poets, builders, rulers who were merciful and rulers who failed. The modern centuries, the houses of prayer, the holy days, kept across all of it.

And these last days drew the lessons: unity builds, knowledge as worship, ordinary hands, mercy remembered, failures admitted, women who were there, many faces, the prayer that went on, back to the source, his character, history held lightly, what you'll leave, and the chain.

Whatever brought you here, faith, curiosity, a partner, a parent, you have now heard the long story, and in the loose sense of yesterday's chain, whoever hears a story and passes some of it on becomes part of it.

how: Muslims often make du'a for those who came before them in faith, using words like Qur'an 59:10, and many keep alive the names of the Prophet's companions and the scholars who followed by reading their lives.

games.q: you've reached the end of a long history, full of the righteous and the failures. what does the Qur'an show later believers doing about those who came before?
games.why: Qur'an 59:10 describes them asking forgiveness for their brethren who came before them in the faith.

practice: Bring back a few faces from this year: Khadijah, Bilal, Fatima, Husayn, a scholar in Baghdad, a woman who founded a school, a grandmother you'll never know by name.
In the Qur'an, later believers are described praying for those before them, in Pickthall's words: "Our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith."
If you pray, you can say that line for all of them; if not, simply hold the long line of people in your mind.

wordCard.voice: Karbala, the hard chapter of the succession and the first split, remembered with Sunni and Shia memory side by side. Today's word.
